name: Henadad
overview: Henadad was a male Levite known primarily as the father of Binnui, as recorded in Nehemiah. He is mentioned among the Levites who sealed the covenant document in Nehemiah 10, highlighting his role within the priestly tribe during the post-exilic period. His identification as a Levite situates him within the tribe responsible for temple service and religious duties.
namesAndTitles: The name Henadad means 'favor of Hadad,' reflecting a proper name of Semitic origin. This name is not indicated as given by God, but it carries a theophoric element referencing Hadad, an ancient deity, which was common in Hebrew names of the period.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Henadad as the father of Binnui, another Levite, establishing a direct familial link within the tribe of Levi. No other family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Henadad's significance lies in his association with the Levites who committed to the covenant renewal in Nehemiah 10, demonstrating his participation in the communal dedication to God's law after the exile. His mention on the sealed document underscores his standing among the faithful Levites who supported the restoration of proper worship and covenant fidelity in Jerusalem.
